_meta.purpose: Circuit profiles for the Weather Whiplash drying-rate and tire-strategy engine.

provenance.surface_type: Objectively verifiable. Street circuits are public roads; permanent circuits are purpose-built.
provenance.shade: Observable from broadcast footage. Affects how much sun reaches the surface.
provenance.climate: Verifiable from location. Drives typical humidity and ambient temperature.
provenance.severity: OUR OWN categorisation, inferred from Pirelli's published compound nominations - harder compounds are brought to higher-severity circuits. Pirelli does not publish raw abrasiveness numbers.
provenance.lap_time_s: MEASURED via FastF1 (2026-08-11): median green-flag race lap, excluding pit, safety-car and opening laps.
provenance.pit_loss_s: MEASURED via FastF1 (2026-08-11): median of (in-lap + out-lap) - 2 x driver's own median green-flag lap, green-flag stops only.
provenance.typical_weather: ESTIMATED typical race-day conditions, not measured. Used as defaults so each circuit starts from plausible values instead of one global guess. Override per request, or fetch live conditions using lat/lon.
provenance.lat_lon: Circuit coordinates, for optional live weather lookup.

_meta.display_rule: Never show C-numbers in the UI. Compound colours are relative to the three compounds nominated for a given race, so any fixed C-number to colour mapping is wrong at most events. Show Soft / Medium / Hard.
_meta.selection_note: Ten circuits chosen to span the full behavioural range - fastest to slowest drying, most to least abrasive. More circuits add no new behaviour to demonstrate.

bahrain.name: Bahrain International Circuit
bahrain.notes: Fastest drying on the list AND among the most abrasive - the two axes are independent. Granite-aggregate surface drives high degradation; Pirelli brings the hardest compounds. Desert dust can confuse the vision model.

jeddah.name: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
jeddah.notes: Street layout but very smooth and fast. Heat offsets the poorer street drainage.

suzuka.name: Suzuka International Racing Course
suzuka.notes: Among the highest tire loads on the calendar. Intermediates overheat quickly once a dry line forms.

miami.name: Miami International Autodrome
miami.notes: Poor street drainage combined with high humidity. Water pools and clears slowly.

monaco.name: Circuit de Monaco
monaco.notes: Slowest drying on the list. Public road drainage, buildings blocking sun and wind, tunnel section stays damp. Be conservative recommending slicks here.

montreal.name: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
montreal.notes: Park circuit on public roads, smooth and low-abrasion - Pirelli brings the softest compounds on the calendar. The tire issue here is graining and warm-up, not wear. Frequently changeable weather.

silverstone.name: Silverstone Circuit
silverstone.notes: Open airfield - excellent drainage, full sun and wind exposure. Dry line forms fast. High lateral loads.

spa.name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
spa.notes: Longest lap. Genuine microclimates - one sector can be wet while another is dry. The best argument for per-sector monitoring.

zandvoort.name: Circuit Zandvoort
zandvoort.notes: Steeply banked corners (Tarzan, Arie Luyendyk) load the tires heavily - Pirelli brings hard compounds. Coastal wind accelerates drying. Blown sand can look like drying patches: a known vision failure mode.

singapore.name: Marina Bay Street Circuit
singapore.notes: Night race, very high humidity, street drainage, buildings on all sides. Drying nearly stalls - the strongest test of the humidity term.

_estimated.note: lap_time_s and pit_loss_s are typical published values, not FastF1-measured. Run tools/refresh_circuits.py to replace with measured data.
